Weekend reflections: $NVDA hit +32.5% this week after 45 days. 

The lesson here isn't the gain - it's that good setups take time to work. When I was starting out, I'd exit winners way too early because I was scared of giving back profits.

Breaking down Friday's new signals: $AMPX and $LUMN both cleared all 5 gates.

Both are AI infrastructure plays - the picks behind the picks. Not the flashy AI names everyone talks about, but the companies building the actual backbone.

https://sterlingsignals.substack.com

Honest question for the weekend: How many of you actually wait for your thesis to play out vs getting impatient and moving to the next shiny object?

Asking because past me definitely had ADHD when it came to holding positions 📚

Here's the thing about data center plays like $LUMN - they're not sexy. No one's making TikToks about fiber infrastructure.

But AI needs massive power and connectivity. Someone has to provide it. That's often where the real money gets made.

This week: 2 new signals, one big winner hitting new highs.

I wish someone told me early on that consistency beats perfection every time. You don't need to catch every move - just the right ones.

Power grids, cooling systems, real estate. The picks and shovels approach might be where the real money is.

End of day thought: every losing trade taught me something that made the next winner possible.

Not saying losses are fun. But they're not wasted if you actually learn from them.

Mid-week check: still sticking to your rules?

It's easy to follow your plan when things are going well. The real test is when you're bored, tempted, or second-guessing yourself.

Discipline isn't a one-time decision. It's choosing the same boring thing every day.

Something I notice with newer traders: they want to understand everything before they start.

But you can't learn to swim by reading about water.

Start small. Make mistakes. Learn from them. Repeat.
